declared.title: Effects of Choice Set Sizes and Moderations of Anxiety and State Emotions on Mental Health Self-Care Uptake, Engagement, and User Experience: Experimental Study
declared.foundIn: rapport contre-preuve reports/too-many-choices/counter-evidence.md (2026-11-22), DOI trouvé par ses requêtes ; titre relevé sur Crossref par la session : contrôle d'identité plus faible ; déjà vue par la recherche Europe PMC « choice overload … culture OR moderator » du dossier

population: 652 adults recruited by university e-mail and social media (authors in Hong Kong), randomly offered 1, 4 or 16 self-care exercises

findings.text: Offering 4 or 16 self-care exercises rather than 1 made people more likely to practise one and more satisfied with their decision

support.sentence: Presenting multiple choices resulted in a higher likelihood of practice (odds ratio 3.12, 95% CI 2.08 to 4.67 and 3.83, 95% CI 2.55 to 5.76; P<.001) and better decision satisfaction (16-choice vs 1-choice: d=0.36, 95% CI 0.17 to 0.56, P<.001; 4-choice vs 1-choice: d=0.24, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.43, P=.03) compared with presenting with a single choice.

limits: 1, 4 or 16 options only: says nothing about very large sets
self-care exercises in an online study
effect stored is 16 vs 1 choice (decision satisfaction); the abstract gives no 16 vs 4 test
the abstract's moderation result (anxious people more satisfied with 16) is in a sentence too long to keep: not used
